chunks: Some of the rustics take whatever they spend as a penalty, and wait for an adverse turn in your fortune. For them will be the adverse change, as God hears all and knows everything.
ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'waiting for the turns of fortune' in Surah At-Tawbah?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the psychological state of the Bedouins who viewed charitable spending as a financial burden rather than a spiritual investment, reflecting their superficial faith. Their expectation of 'turns of fortune' (al-dawair) underscores a transactional view of divine reward, where they anticipated immediate worldly compensation for their sacrifices. This contrasts with the Shia emphasis on sincere intention (niyyah) and patience (sabr) in the path of God.
